title: Reduce false-positive burn escalations by introducing impact-weighted paging and spike decay
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: During the 2026-01-28 capacity regression we observed an explosion of burn-rate pagers. Many pages were triggered by short-lived spikes originating from a single noisy tenant and by KV cache warmup churn. The current burn alerting logic is largely absolute and region-wide which results in high signal fan-out and significant oncall noise.

Goal: Reduce false-positive burn-rate escalations and overall pager noise while preserving SLO breach visibility for customer-impacting events. We want to make paging decisions sensitive to (1) sustained breach duration, (2) estimated customer-impact weight, and (3) transient spike smoothing, without blinding ourselves to multi-tenant incidents.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Introduce an impact-weighted paging threshold: compute a lightweight impact score per alerting window (based on number of unique customer keys affected, percent of capacity per-customer, and request error-rate) and require a minimum impact score to escalate to pager.
2) Add spike-decay smoothing to the burn signal: apply an exponential decay window (configurable half-life) so single-sample spikes do not immediately escalate.
3) Add a soft-alert tier: emit a non-pager channel (dashboard and slack non-pager) for short, low-impact breaches. Only escalate to pager if either impact score or duration threshold is exceeded.
4) Group similar signals by noisy-dimension (tenant_id, model_variant, region) to reduce duplicate pages and aggregate root-cause context in the page.
5) Preserve rapid escalation for high-severity multi-customer outages by bypassing smoothing when error-rates exceed an absolute threshold (failsafe).

Why this is different from previous work: prior tickets focused primarily on burn hysteresis and windowing. This ticket combines customer-impact weighting, explicit spike-decay smoothing, and grouping to reduce duplicated pages while retaining fast escalation for high-impact outages.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Risk of delayed escalation for a genuine short, high-impact outage if impact scoring is miscalibrated. Mitigation: failsafe absolute thresholds and staged rollout with tight monitoring.
- Added compute cost in alert pipeline for impact scoring and grouping. Mitigation: implement lightweight approximations and sample-based scoring for high-cardinality metrics.
- Complexity in root-cause debugging if grouping logic is too aggressive. Mitigation: include ungrouped raw signal in page payload and a link to the grouped context view.
acceptance_criteria: Pager count per incident reduced by >=50% for incidents driven by single-tenant spikes (measured over 30d window).
No increase in average SLO breach duration for customer-impacting incidents (target: <=5% change).
Soft-alerts surface on Console with clear links to grouped context and runbook.
Canary region rollout for 2 weeks with no missed high-impact escalations (verified by synthetic canaries and retrospective review).
Runbook updated and oncall training completed prior to broad rollout.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize impact score formula and spike-decay half-life (SRE+Metrics) — due 2026-02-18.
Instrumentation: add lightweight per-window impact counters and tag propagation (metrics team) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics/pull/1784.
Alerting pipeline: update signal-transform service to apply exponential decay and compute impact score; implement grouping heuristics (ENG).
Testing: add unit tests for decay math, integration tests with synthetic time-series, and stress test grouping with high-cardinality synthetic traffic (staging).
Canary rollout: enable in secondary region for 2 weeks; monitor PagerCount, MeanTimeToDetect, and SLO breach durations; collect feedback.
Full rollout: gradual enabling across regions with 24h monitoring windows and rollback knobs.
notes: Prototype PR implementing decay: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/pull/402 — initial benchmarks show ~8% extra CPU on pipeline at peak when scoring enabled; optimization planned.
